own_scenes.family: Nueva York: Def Jam, Queens y la edad de oro
own_scenes.desc: Nasir Jones asombró a los diecisiete años con su estrofa en «Live at the Barbeque» de Main Source («I went to hell for snuffin’ Jesus»). Large Professor, el Obi-Wan Kenobi discreto de los productores, quería esperar; Simmons lo rechazó por sonar a Kool G Rap; Faith Newman lo fichó para Columbia por medio de MC Serch. Illmatic (abril de 1994), diez temas grabados en dos años y medio mientras lloraba a su amigo Ill Will, reunió por primera vez en un disco a los mejores productores de Nueva York (DJ Premier, Q-Tip, Large Professor, Pete Rock y L.E.S.): rimas internas de varias sílabas como nadie desde Rakim, un niño en la portada, un sample de Wild Style en «The Genesis» frente a la comercialidad de Hammer y Vanilla Ice. «N.Y. State of Mind», la primera rima perfecta. Con The Infamous de Mobb Deep abrió la segunda edad de oro de Queensbridge.

refs.q: I went to Large Professor to ask him about this kid, Nasty Nas.
refs.para: I went to Large Professor to ask him about this kid, Nasty Nas. And he felt at the time that he was trying to push [Queens artist] Akinyele out there first and wait on Nas, and that’s not really where my head was at.

refs.q: Fuck, this guy is a fucking genius and if it takes two years to make an album, then that’s what it’s going to take because it’ll be worth it.
refs.para: I was feeling very upset [one] night, but he had left his rhyme book behind, so I picked it up and started reading it, and I said, “Fuck, this guy is a fucking genius and if it takes two years to make an album, then that’s what it’s going to take because it’ll be worth it.”

refs.q: It’s basically the first perfect rhyme.
refs.para: I think it’s one of the greatest produced. It’s scored correct—the intonation, the feeling, the vibe, everything. It’s basically the first perfect rhyme.
